context.text: After His Resurrection Christ showed Himself to the apostles, "being seen of them forty days", and commanded them "that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father". When He had been taken up from the mount called Olivet, they returned to the city and kept together in an upper room with "the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren", about a hundred and twenty in all. There they chose Matthias to take the place of Judas.

Pentecost, the fiftieth day, was the feast of weeks. The Law of Moses counted seven weeks from the offering of the first sheaf, and on the fiftieth day a new offering was brought to the Lord at "the beginning of wheat-harvest". It was one of the three feasts at which every man of Israel was to appear before the Lord, and Acts records that there were dwelling at Jerusalem "Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven".

narrative.text: The feast fell ten days after the Ascension, as St Augustine reckons the forty days and the fifty. Acts tells what happened in the house where the disciples were gathered, and describes the coming of the Spirit as something both heard and seen:

And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.

The sound drew a crowd, and the pilgrims were amazed that men of Galilee were speaking their own languages. "Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia", people of Judaea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and Libya, visitors from Rome, Cretans and Arabians all heard them tell "the wonderful works of God". Others mocked, and said the men were "full of new wine".

Peter stood up with the eleven and answered that it was only "the third hour of the day". This, he said, was what the prophet Joel had foretold: "I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh". He preached Jesus of Nazareth, crucified and raised up by God, "whereof we all are witnesses"; exalted at God's right hand, Jesus had received the promised Spirit from the Father and poured it out on them. "God hath made that same Jesus, whom ye have crucified, both Lord and Christ."

The hearers "were pricked in their heart" and asked what they should do. Peter answered: "Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost." Those who received his word were baptized, "and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls." Acts then sets down the shape of the new community's life:
And they continued stedfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.

They went daily to the temple, broke bread in their homes and held their goods in common, sharing them as each had need, and "fear came upon every soul: and many wonders and signs were done by the apostles." The chapter ends: "And the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved."

significance.text: The Orthodox Church keeps the feast on the fiftieth day after Pascha. It calls the Sunday the Day of the Holy Trinity and keeps the Day of the Spirit on the Monday after. Its troparion blesses Christ "who hast revealed fishers most wise, sending down upon them the Holy Spirit, and thereby catching the universe as in a net." The kontakion reads the gift of tongues against the tower of Babel:

When the Most High confounded the tongues, he dispersed the nations: but when he distributed the tongues of fire, he called all men unto unity. Wherefore, with one accord, we glorify the All-holy Spirit.
significance.source: Kontakion of Pentecost, in the Service Book, tr. Isabel F. Hapgood (1906), p. 247

significance.text: The fathers read the day as the fulfilment of the Law's Pentecost. St Augustine set the two side by side: after the first Passover "after 50 days the Law is given, which inspires fear, written by the finger of God", and after Christ's Passover "after 50 days is given the Holy Spirit, who is the finger of God, and whose fruit is love". At every Divine Liturgy the priest, praying over the bread and wine, still asks God to "send thy Holy Spirit upon us, and upon these Gifts here spread forth".

consequences.text: From Jerusalem the witness went out as the risen Christ had said it would, "both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth." Acts follows it to Samaria, where Peter and John prayed for the baptized to receive the Holy Ghost, and to the house of Cornelius, where the Spirit fell on Gentiles as Peter spoke. The question that followed, whether Gentile believers must keep the Law of Moses, brought the apostles and elders together at Jerusalem.

uncertainty: Acts gives no year. The date depends on the year of the Crucifixion, which the Gospels do not state; Luke fixes only the start of John the Baptist's preaching, "in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar" (Luke 3:1). The date of about 33 shown here is the conventional one, not a documented civil date. Acts does not say whether "they were all" in 2:1 means the twelve or the whole company of about a hundred and twenty; St John Chrysostom held that the Spirit came "upon the hundred and twenty". The link between the fiftieth day and the giving of the Law at Sinai is a reading of the fathers, made here from St Augustine, and is not stated in Acts.

people.name: St Peter the Apostle
people.role: Stood up with the eleven and preached the sermon of Pentecost, after which about three thousand were baptized.

people.name: The Most Holy Theotokos
people.role: Named in Acts among those who continued in prayer with the apostles in the days before Pentecost.

people.name: St John the Apostle
people.role: One of the eleven in the upper room; soon after, Peter's companion in Jerusalem and in Samaria.

people.name: St Matthias the Apostle
people.role: Chosen by lot in place of Judas shortly before Pentecost and numbered with the eleven.

people.name: The Prophet Joel
people.role: Foretold that God would pour out His Spirit upon all flesh; Peter declared the prophecy fulfilled that day.

review.basis: Rests on Acts 1-2 (King James Version) and the Septuagint passages on the feast of weeks (Brenton), with the hymns of the feast and the Liturgy from Hapgood's Service Book of 1906 and readings of St Augustine and St John Chrysostom in their NPNF translations. Quotations are verbatim; the rest is our paraphrase of Acts.
